connect.title: Connect
connect.text: Link your Cloudflare account, your GitHub repository and your Anthropic key. Your keys go straight to your own account.

ask.title: Ask
ask.text: Describe the change the way you'd explain it to a developer, on Telegram or on the web.

review.title: Review
review.text: The agent edits the code in an isolated environment and sends you the staging link. Iterate as many times as you like.

approve.title: Approve
approve.text: One tap opens the PR, merges it and GitHub Actions ships it. Something went wrong? {command} brings back the previous version.

selfHosted.title: Your bohr, on your infrastructure
selfHosted.text: bohr is open source under the MIT license. Install your own instance in your Cloudflare account in minutes and use it with your team or your clients.

bullets.deploy: The Deploy to Cloudflare button or {command}
bullets.multi: One instance for many users and projects
bullets.noLockIn: No dependency on bohr.io: the code is yours

accounts.title: Everything runs in your accounts
accounts.text: The instance is a thin control plane. Each project's code, data and messages stay in the user's own accounts, and every provider is paid directly.
accounts.diagram: Diagram of how bohr connects to your accounts
accounts.footnote: The instance only stores your Cloudflare token, encrypted, and the GitHub App installation.

security.title: You decide what goes to production
security.approval: Nothing reaches production without approval: every change goes through a staging environment with its own URL.
security.members: Owner and members: invite people with a code and revoke access whenever you want.
security.sandbox: Each project gets its own isolated sandbox; nothing is shared between projects.
security.tokens: Least-privilege tokens, encrypted, with every use logged.
security.rollback: Roll back with a single command.

stack.title: Bring your stack
stack.text: When you import a project, the agent reads the repository and decides where each piece runs. Anything without a home becomes a warning, never a broken deploy.
stack.caption: Where each piece of your repository runs

plans.title: Choose how to use it
plans.note: Prices in US dollars. On both plans, you pay for infrastructure (Cloudflare and Anthropic tokens) directly to the providers.

customers.title: Already a bohr customer?
customers.text: Your projects already run on the new version, with the same domains and the same price. To use the agent, just add your Anthropic key. Whenever you want, move each project to your own Cloudflare account from the panel.

community.title: Built with the community
community.text: bohr is built in public. Join in on GitHub and chat with the team on Discord.
community.contributors: People who have contributed to bohr

needCode.question: Do I need to know how to code?
needCode.answer: Not to request changes: you describe what you want and approve the result. To install your own instance, it helps to know the basics of Cloudflare and GitHub.

cost.question: How much does it cost?
cost.answer: Self-hosted is free; the agent needs Cloudflare's Workers Paid plan (US$5/month) on your account. bohr.io Cloud costs US$20/month and works with a free Cloudflare account. Either way, you pay for your infrastructure directly to the providers: what your sites use on Cloudflare, container usage when the agent runs in your account, and Anthropic tokens.

data.question: Where does my data live?
data.answer: In your accounts. The code lives in your GitHub, projects run in your Cloudflare account and databases live in your Neon or Upstash. The instance only stores your Cloudflare token, encrypted.

telegram.question: Does it work without Telegram?
telegram.answer: Yes. The web interface has the same chat as the bot, with the staging preview right next to it.

model.question: Which AI model does the agent use?
model.answer: Claude, by Anthropic, with your own key. You choose the model for each project.

mistakes.question: What if the AI gets it wrong?
mistakes.answer: Nothing goes to production without your approval. You review everything on staging, ask for changes or discard it. After shipping, {command} brings back the previous version.

difference.question: What's the difference between self-hosted and Cloud?
difference.answer: With self-hosted, you install and run the instance. With Cloud, bohr runs the instance for you. In both, your projects run in your Cloudflare account.
